difficulties: None blocking. (1) The Makefile hard-codes mechanisms/ts1.json and --symbol ts1, so the route is the temporary swap; the benchmark drivers resolve CSV columns and output species by name, so they run any mechanism unchanged. (2) The converter must declare 'rate units: mol m-3'; the reader's default is molecule cm-3, which would silently rescale A, k0_A and kinf_A. (3) With 4 cells the single group has 4 cells, not the generated stride of 32, so bin/ts1_bench_specialized ran the generic rate, forcing, Jacobian, LU and triangular-solve kernels (the documented fallback); the generated kernels ran only with 64 cells (two 32-cell groups) or after rebuilding with the Makefile's GROUP_SIZE=4. (4) make env creates a fresh conda environment from conda-forge with a repo-local package cache (network needed); it was run offline (CONDA_OFFLINE=true) after seeding .conda_pkgs from this entry's earlier exercise worktree. (5) /usr/bin/make is GNU Make 3.81 (whole-second mtimes): a swap within the same second as the previous build is not seen as newer; the timed rebuilds therefore pause 1.1 s before each swap and every build log was checked for the full regenerate/compile/link sequence.
code_path_evidence: src/ts1_bench.c:16-20 sets group_size = CHEM_GROUP_SIZE (-DCHEM_GROUP_SIZE=32 for the specialized binary) and caps it at the cell count; src/ts1_driver.h:19-20,35 maps chem_update_rates/chem_solve to ts1_update_rates/ts1_solve and calls ts1_specialized_attach, which installs the generated factor/solve as s->linear (called at src/rosenbrock_step.inc:44,63 with s->cells). In each generated file (runs/MECH/specialized.c; CB5 line numbers) ts1_update_rates: 'if (s->cells!=32) chem_update_rates(s); else rates(s);' (4205), forcing: 'if (s->cells!=32) { chem_forcing(s,y,f); return; }' (6859), Jacobian: '#define chem_solver_negative_jacobian(s,state,y) ((s)->cells==32 ? jacobian(...) : chem_solver_negative_jacobian(...))' (15641), factor: 'if (n!=32) return chem_lu_factor(...)' (13939), solve: 'if (n!=32) { chem_lu_solve(...); return; }' (15361). 4 cells: one 4-cell group, so generic kernels; 64 cells: two 32-cell groups, so generated kernels. Confirmed at run time with clang profile counters in an instrumented copy built in coverage/ from the same sources and generated C (results identical to the real runs).
